Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines · Body, health & movement

knee noun

also knees

classical

genū, genūs n.; plural genua

noun, fourth declension

knee; knees

The nominative genū has a long ū; all three vowels of the plural genua are short.

Examples

  • Genua flecte.

    Bend your knees.composed

  • Ubi genū tuum est?

    Where is your knee?composed

See also bend, foot, hand, leg.

SourcesLewis & Short: genu · Allen & Greenough §10a: vowel quantity before another vowel

The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
